questions.q: What must exist before an expdp or impdp job can run?
options: An open RMAN channel
A recovery catalog registration
A wallet/keystore for the target schema
A database directory object pointing to a server-side OS path, referenced by name
questions.explain: Data Pump jobs run server-side and reference dump file locations through a named directory object, not a raw client-side path.

questions.q: What does REMAP_SCHEMA=hr:hr_staging do during an impdp job?
options: Filters the import to only staging-related tables
Encrypts the imported data using the hr_staging wallet
Loads the exported objects into the hr_staging schema instead of the original hr schema
Renames the hr schema permanently in the source database
questions.explain: REMAP_SCHEMA is the standard way to load a production export into a different target schema, such as for refreshing test/staging.

questions.q: Which Data Pump option would filter an export down to only rows from the last 30 days within a table?
options: REMAP_TABLESPACE=
DIRECTORY=
QUERY=
PARALLEL=
questions.explain: QUERY= filters which rows within an exported table are included, something RMAN has no equivalent for.

questions.q: Why can't RMAN accomplish a job like 'export just the orders table, filtered to the last 30 days, into a differently-named schema'?
options: RMAN only works with Data Pump dump files as its source
RMAN requires a recovery catalog before any selective operation
RMAN backs up physical files at the block level and has no concept of exporting selected rows or remapping schemas
RMAN can do this, it just requires the CUMULATIVE option
questions.explain: This is precisely the class of job that distinguishes logical export (Data Pump) from physical, block-level backup (RMAN).

questions.q: What does this lesson conclude about the relationship between RMAN and Data Pump?
options: Data Pump is simply a wrapper around RMAN commands
They are not competing tools — a real production environment schedules both, for different jobs
RMAN is only used for development environments, Data Pump for production
Data Pump has fully replaced RMAN in modern Oracle versions
questions.explain: RMAN handles physical disaster recovery and point-in-time restore; Data Pump handles logical, selective, portable migration — both are needed.
